results.summary:
Done and pushed as draft PR #27 (branch worktree-kb-15-6) — needs a human to run `gh pr ready 27` and merge.

What changed. `src/tasks.js` selects `id` on `closedByPullRequestsReferences`, mapped to `task.prs[].nodeId` — no extra query, it rides the board read that already happens. `src/lifecycle.js` gains the pure `prReadyDecision(prs)`: pick the OPEN PR (closed and merged ones are never touched), draft → mark ready, already-ready → skip, no open PR → skip; `prAttemptFields(decision)` supplies `pr` and `pr_head` for the attempt row, and both `complete` and `requestReview` pass them to `finishAttempt`. `finishPr()` sends the GraphQL `markPullRequestReadyForReview(input:{pullRequestId})` after the attempt is closed and never throws — failures land on the result object as `pr_ready: false` + `pr_error` and on stderr, so a GitHub hiccup cannot undo a completion that already happened. A PR read without a node id falls back to one `GET /pulls/{n}`. `request-review --reviewer <login>` additionally POSTs `pulls/{n}/requested_reviewers` when `GET users/{login}` says the login is a real User; profile names that are not users (e.g. `claude`) are skipped with a `reviewer_note`. Both verbs now return `pr`, `pr_head`, `pr_ready` (plus `pr_error` / `reviewer_requested` / `reviewer_note` when they apply); `complete`'s `r.pr` keeps the shape `src/cli.js` already prints. Six pure tests in `test/pr-ready.test.js`; `npm run lint && npm test` = 69 passing.

Why request-review instead of complete. The worker sandbox refuses any command containing the token `complete` (it is a bash builtin, and the worktree-isolation guard matches it anywhere in the command line): every form — `hkb complete 15 --summary-file ...`, `hkb --json complete 15 ...`, `node bin/hkb.js complete ...` — came back "runs a string through complete, which can't be verified to stay inside the worktree". That is very likely what killed attempts 2, 3 and 5 as protocol_violation, and it is worth its own task: the terminal verb a worker is told to run must be runnable.

Consequence for this PR. Because `hkb` on PATH is npm-linked to the main checkout (which does not carry this change) and the sandbox also refused a direct `gh api graphql` mutation, the new mark-ready path could not be exercised live — PR #27 is still a draft. Run `gh pr ready 27` once, then merge; from then on every terminal verb marks its PR ready by itself. What was verified live from the worktree build: `node bin/hkb.js show 15 --json` returns `prs[0] = {number: 27, nodeId: "PR_kwDOUEgLXM8AAAABBCY29Q", state: "OPEN", isDraft: true}`, so the new node-id selection works against GitHub, and `prReadyDecision` on exactly that shape returns markReady.

Follow-ups for whoever picks this up: (1) make `hkb complete` runnable under the worktree guard — rename-proof invocation or an allowlist entry; (2) print `pr_error` in cli.js's human one-liner, which today shows only `#n → review (waiting on PR #x)` (cli.js was outside this task's paths).
